This is ungraded practice. It turns the Session 3 workflow into a complete mini-project: a scalar ODE, its equilibrium structure, numerical integration and an interactive front end [@strogatz2024nonlinear, Section 3.7].

Use these pages as guides:

[Budworm: the Model in Code](budworm-implementation.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Budworm: Integration and Time Series](budworm-integration.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Budworm: a Streamlit App](budworm-streamlit.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

## Goals

Your work should show that you can:

- implement the budworm model and its plots;
- build an app that evolves the dynamics correctly;
- interpret equilibria, bistability and hysteresis.

## Tasks

- Implement `spruce_budworm()` and the plotting helpers.
- Build a Streamlit app with the rate plot, the time series and an "Evolve" button.
- Use `st.session_state` so the simulation persists across interactions.
- Answer at least three of the [experiment questions](budworm-integration.qmd#sec-exploration-questions), with figures.

## Short discussion

Write a few paragraphs that answer:

- How many equilibria appear for the parameter values you explored?
- Did different initial conditions converge to different long-run states?
- Did you observe hysteresis or threshold behaviour?

::: {.callout-tip}
## Optional extension
- Put the project in a GitHub repository with a short report.
- Deploy the app and share the link.
- Add a reset button or multiple trajectories.
- Implement Euler or a Runge-Kutta method yourself and compare with SciPy.
:::

## Tips

- Start with the ODE and the static plots before you build the app.
- Test each function separately.
- Keep the session state logic simple before adding features.
- Compare with the reference code in [amlab/odes_1d/spruce_budworm.py](https://github.com/daniprec/BAM-Applied-Math-Lab/blob/main/amlab/odes_1d/spruce_budworm.py).
